title: You Get a Brand New Skeleton Every 10 Years

scenes.text: The skeleton inside you right now is not the one you had ten years ago.
Your bones aren't dead scaffolding. They're living tissue, constantly being torn down and rebuilt.
Special cells chew away old bone, and others lay down fresh bone in its place. All day, every day.
The US Surgeon General's report on bone health says most of the adult skeleton is replaced about every ten years.
It happens so your bones can repair tiny cracks from daily life and release calcium when your body needs it.
So what you eat and how you move today is building the skeleton you'll stand on in ten years.

description:
The skeleton inside you right now is not the one you had ten years ago.
Bone is living tissue. Special cells break down old bone and others rebuild it, and most of the adult skeleton is replaced about every ten years.
This constant remodeling repairs tiny cracks and keeps calcium flowing to the rest of your body.
What would you change today if you knew it was building your bones for 2036?
